company.name: Quarrender Ellingtree LLP
company.blurb: An estate and business-planning law firm of 16 people: three partners, three associates, four paralegals, three legal assistants and an office team of three. Its weeks run on matters, time entries, calendar dates and documents chased from clients, the same rhythm an accounting firm knows from engagements and due dates.

playbooks.label: Monthly pre-bills and invoices
playbooks.summary: Chases missing time before the pre-bills run, lists each partner's pre-bills for review, and follows up unpaid invoices at 30 and 60 days. Partners approve; billing issues the invoices.

playbooks.label: Client funds reconciliation
playbooks.summary: Lines up the adjusted bank balance, the trust account journal and the total of the matter ledgers each month, for billing to prepare and the managing partner to sign off. Read-only.

playbooks.label: Weekly docket review
playbooks.summary: Lists every date on the calendar for the coming weeks with who is on each matter and whether court dates were checked by the responsible lawyer. Lawyers decide every deadline.

playbooks.label: New matter intake
playbooks.summary: Runs every name on an intake against the firm's records for a lawyer to review, then tracks the engagement letter until it is signed and back.

playbooks.label: Document requests to clients
playbooks.summary: Tracks each document requested from a client, with reminders a week after the request and every two weeks after that.

playbooks.label: Client status updates
playbooks.summary: Drafts a status note from the matter record and the request list, for the lawyer to review and send.

questions.ask: Which prospective clients are waiting for a conflict check, and what in our records matches each name?
questions.reply: Three prospective clients are waiting for a conflict check. Every name on their intakes was searched against our records, and four of the eight names match a record: Sunniva and Arne Bratlie both match a former client, Ingeborg Bratlie; Lysander Coe, an owner of Pennick Hollow Farms, is the adverse party in a current dispute; and Orrisdale Veterinary Group, the seller of the building, is a current client. A lawyer reviews each match and decides. Dates of birth taken at intake stay blacked out.
questions.before: Intake ran each name through the firm's records and the lawyer pieced the matches together before deciding.
questions.now: Every name on each waiting intake, searched against clients, adverse parties and other parties to our matters, with the matter each match sits on. A lawyer decides.

questions.ask: Who has working days last week with no time entered?
questions.reply: Three working days last week have no time entered. Thaddeus Wrenfold has none for Wednesday and Thursday. Imani Castellow has none yet for Friday, which under our procedure is due by the end of today. Days marked out of office on the calendar are left off the list.
questions.before: Chasing missing time meant scanning each person's week in the billing system before the next pre-bills ran.
questions.now: Every working day with no time entered, by person, leaving out days marked out of office on the calendar.

questions.ask: List unpaid invoices, oldest first.
questions.reply: {n} unpaid invoices, oldest first. Most were issued in the last month, many of them flat fees billed after recent signings. Five are more than 30 days old, and each has had its reminder under our procedure. The oldest, a September flat fee, has had both reminders and is now for the responsible lawyer to call about. For hourly matters, the client funds column shows what each matter holds; applying funds to an invoice waits for the responsible lawyer. Click a matter to open its record.
questions.before: Following up unpaid invoices meant running an aged list and checking each one against payments and reminders.
questions.now: Every unpaid invoice with its age, its last reminder and the client funds held for the matter, from billing and the trust records. The assistant cannot record a payment or apply funds.

questions.ask: Where do the trust account reconciliations stand, and do the matter ledgers add up to the account?
questions.reply: The last three monthly reconciliations of the trust account. In each, the adjusted bank balance, the trust account journal and the total of the matter ledgers agree, with no difference. September and October are signed off by Odessa Quarrender. November's is prepared and waiting for her review; its $10,000 in deposits in transit is a further advance received on November 30 that cleared the next working day.
questions.before: Billing prepares each reconciliation from the bank statement, the journal and the matter ledgers, and the managing partner signs it off.
questions.now: Each month's three figures side by side, with who prepared and who signed off, read from the trust records. The assistant does not reconcile the account or move funds.

Rowan Achterhof

questions.ask: What does our procedure say about putting a court date or deadline on the calendar?
questions.reply: Every hearing, mediation, response date and filing date goes on the calendar the day we learn of it, from the court's notice or order. The paralegal on the matter enters it, and the responsible lawyer checks it against the notice and initials it. The lawyer decides every deadline. questions.now: The answer comes from the firm's own procedure, with the section shown.

result.query: court deadline hearing notice initials docket

results.heading: Entering a court date or deadline
results.text:
## Entering a court date or deadline

Every hearing, mediation, response date and filing date goes on the calendar the day we learn of it, from the court's notice or order or the other side's papers. The paralegal on the matter enters it, and the responsible lawyer checks the entry against the notice and initials it in the calendar. The lawyer decides every deadline. Nobody, and no tool, works out a deadline on their own.

results.heading: Weekly docket review
results.text:
## Weekly docket review

Each Monday the managing partner reviews the dates on the calendar for the next two weeks with the lawyers on each matter, so that nothing comes due without the work being ready.

questions.now: Each seat's access is listed in one place: what it can read, what it can change and what is withheld.
